Our team works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. You don't have to sort through this alone or guess what to say to an adjuster.

whyChoose.title: What Montebello Drivers Should Know Before Talking to an Insurer

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim in California, though claims against a government entity (like certain road defect cases) can require notice in as little as six months. Missing these windows can end your ability to recover, so it helps to talk to someone early.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Automatically Sink Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the crash — your share of fault simply reduces the amount. Our team can help make sure fault isn't overstated against you.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: Unlike some states, California doesn't cap non-economic damages such as pain and suffering in most car accident cases. That's one reason it's worth having someone evaluate the full picture of your losses before accepting an early settlement offer.

items.question: Should I give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement?
items.answer: It's best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers often use those statements later to minimize what they owe. Our team can talk to the insurer on your behalf.

items.question: Why does the Friday evening timing at SR-60 and Beverly Boulevard matter for my claim?
items.answer: Crash timing and location can affect what evidence is available, such as traffic camera footage or witness recall. Public records show reported collisions in Montebello tend to cluster on Friday evenings around 5-7 p.m., so documenting exact time and location details early can strengthen a claim.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing. We offer a free consultation, and our team works on contingency — meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost or obligation to move forward.
